newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.

text.p: Kirton sacrificed for government unity: Deputy Prime Minister and NZ First leader Winston Peters -- who failed to sack NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan for misleading him in June -- chose on Thursday to sacrifice associate minister Neil Kirton for the sake of coalition unity. Page 1.

Peters keeps options open: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters has left open the possibility that he will not appoint another NZ First minister to keep up his party's quota agreed under the coalition accord. Page 1.
NZ First MPs support axing: NZ First MPs on Thursday stood firmly behind the decision of their leader Winston Peters to sack Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton. Page 2.

Creech on attack over leaked paper: THe leaking of draft paper proposing radical changes for tertiary education has prompted a stinging attack by Education Minister Wyatt Chreech on the honesty and integrity of those responsible. Page 9.

Carter Holt confident on pulp prices: Wallowing pulp prices continued to dog forestry company Carter Holt Harvey, contributing to a 13 percent lower first-quarter tax-paid profit of $49 million. Page 13.

Weak market may keep lid on car prices: Imported car prices may soon rise as a result of the recent fall in the value of the dollar, but a weak car sales market should keep a lid on any increase. Page 13.

Gas suppliers face set of rules to foster competition: Prices for gas in New Zealand are high by international standards, but no one knows if customers are being charged too much, according to Energy Minister Max Bradford. Page 13.

Bolger set to court United and Act: The ruling coalition is likely to take out insurance against the possibility that New Zealand First's sacked minister, Neil Kirton, might become an independent MP by quietly shoring up support from United's Peter Dunne and Act NZ.

Telecom acts to trim charges for ISDN: Telecom has succumbed to user pressure to drop prices for its integrated services digital network (ISDN) and is about to announce plans to replace or upgrade its existing NEC digital exchanges -- seen as a bottleneck in its efforts to connect customers.

Govt stays clear of competition laws inquisition: An inquiry proposed some weeks ago by Alliance MP Laila Harre into the state of competition laws as they affect telecommunications was blocked by the government on Thursday, the MP told the Telecommunications Conference in Auckland.
St Lukes tipped to raise $90m: Shopping mall operator St Lukes Group is tipped to announce a $90 million cash issue or placement this month.
-- The newspaper was not available on Friday in Wellington
